text: Since December 2022, moderation in public areas has been close to non-existing. Staff are generally treating volunteer contributors poorly (and rudely), and has recently started removing posts that are criticizing recent changes and additions. Furthermore, both the apps and the website has been buggy for years. The platforms rely heavily on volunteer work, which is shady considering they are a for-profit company. As a task-management platform, it's okay, but there are other much better.

text: When I started to use habitica I became a big fan of the app. It was my first gamified ToDo/habit management app and I really liked the idea to organise my day like a role play game! Nevertheless, things have changed for me: THE GAMIFICATION My in-game character achieved Level 100 and I played through all the quests Habitica offers in 5 month. Partly, I passed them by myself and other quest I finished with groups of 10+ fellows. For me actually there is no point to play all the quests again or to start again with a level 1 character. And there is more to criticise: I can say that a group of 10+ people makes the quests and the whole game too easy. Your character will become overpowered quite fast: If you have rogues in your group, you will drown in gold and stuff. Warriors can at some point kill most monsters by themselves. Mages are leveling up like crazy and the rest of their group will rarely be out of mana because of their spells. Healers will at some stage avoid any damage for the group but are also very useless in way as long as you can buy a healing potion for 25 Gold. Another critique I have, is about the achievements: They are hard to achieve, which is good in my point of view. Nevertheless they are also quite pointless, because they have NO effect on your game. My conclusion for the gamification part: If you are looking for a gamified todo/habit app Habitica is worth a try, but keep in mind that the gamification part is easily played through and can get quite boring at some stage. Habitica needs i.m.o more balance if you are playing in a group, it needs new (more difficult) quest and achievements which have a real additional value for the gamer. THE TODO/HABIT MANAGEMENT PART: The best thing here is that habitica differentiates between the categories "Habits", "daily/weekly/monthly tasks" and todos. If you are useing habtica with a big screen via browser you can see everything you need to do at a glance. This is really useful! On a smaller screen you need to swipe between the categories, which works quite well. The problem is that the lists in the categories can get quite long even on big screen if you have to manage more than one big project. You can help yourself with specific tags for your tasks and todos and their included checklists. That works but for me it is not the best solution: If you filter one project you lose sight of the other. Here are some features I also really missed: - Reminders cannot be added in the browser version of habitica - If you go on a holiday, there is just the possibilty to pause ALL of your habits, tasks and todos. You cannot pause them by a specific category - There is no easy option to postpone a project, a task or todo (x) hours/days/week etc. You have to change all dates manually - There is no option to limit the duration of specific daily/weekly/monthly tasks for a period of time. My conclusion here: If you need a professional app to manage all yout projects, tasks and habits habitica delivers some good ideas but is lacking quite important features imo. text: Basically every other to-do or habit tracking app wants a subscription to use basic functionality, so I appreciate that this app is functionally free. Unfortunately my brain is hardwired to slack efficiently, and I immediately found a "loophole" in Habitica (literally day one of using it) so I could avoid specific tasks without any negative consequences in the app. As someone who needs a habit tracker because of avoidance, this basically rendered the gimmick of this app useless for me.

text: I much prefer other organizational/self-care apps to this one. Using negative punishment in tandem with positive reinforcement is a major turnoff, and it feels like I gain no real reward. Excellent idea but poor execution. There really isn't much to do game wise 
especially since the majority of the content is locked behind a paywall. I 
understand that they have to monetize it but at 1 million users, ad 
impressions may have been a better route instead of a subscription service 
that locks out the majority of your player base from the start. There's 
also no way to earn crystals other than paying. With so little to do and so 
much unavailable unless you pay (with no options to try before you buy) 
gives me little motivation to come back. Some advice: ●Make the quests you 
can buy with gold cheaper. 200 coins takes forever to grind and there's not 
much to do otherwise. ● Have a way for f2p players to earn crystals (maybe 
through daily login bonuses, level up bonuses or grind and buy them with 
gold). ●Offline capabilities especially for checklists and tasks. I 
shouldn't need the internet to check off my to do list. ●Have the ability 
to choose your class at the start and allow players to change class 
whenever they'd like. Having to wait until you're level 10 is too much of a 
grind. ●Have a little more customization available from the start (maybe a 
freeby starter egg or a background or outfit). Literally everything is 
locked behind crystal pay walls...even the character backgrounds are a 
whopping 15 crystals . That just screams greedy.

text: Wonderful potential and with excellent content but not very well executed. UI poor & buggy; connectivity & state-saving bugs; unintuitive & hazy. However, still a tremendous tool with (I don't use this term lightly) life-changing potential despite! I feel as though the gamification aspect is tangential but foundational to the system design. If the user relies on the superficial static pixel-art RPG as the primary mechanic incentivizing their real-world habits, tasks & challenges, they'll plateau real fast, as there isn't much substance to the 'game' side. The social/game features (custom avatars &c.) are steeply ramped to try to drive pay-for-play schemes, so the appeal to some of a casual showoff/hangout sort of play are curtailed. Some of the user-contributed content (mostly in Challenges but also in general chatpost/Tavern) is excellent; imagine self-help style microlessons but from evidence-based and therapeutically-sound sources, as well as plenty of great personal strategic content and tips from a range of people suffering from a variety of impediments to routine/studying/self-care/productivity/etc. sharing what's worked for them. Incredible, and there's also arts exposure, bookclubbing, hobbyisting, and more being done through the system as well. Bottom line is same as the top: This has awesome potential to (actually) help people improve their lives but the system isn't designed very well and on top of that the app isn't up to professional standards.  Don't have it? Get it, and start it. Try it for a couple weeks if you can. Keep reading...

text: Te ayuda de verdad a crear hábitos. La aplicación es adictiva y entretenida. Vas a estar jugándola en todo momento y cumpliendo así tus metas. Te ofrece una gran posibilidad de personalización de tus tareas: lista de hábitos que quieras incrementar de a pocos, tareas que debas hacer sí o sí todos los días, tareas que solo debes hacer una vez (to-do). Juegas con un avatar y vas agregando oro y experiencia conforme vas cumpliendo tus hábitos. Tienes mascotas, armadura, monturas, fondos. Te enviciaras para tratar de completar tus hábitos para lograr avanzar de nivel. También permite la opción de crear recompensas de modo que si deseas salir a ver una película o con amigos debes haber juntado una cantidad de dinero mínima. Y esa cantidad solo se obtiene realizando hábitos. Las únicas desventajas que le encuentro son que la aplicación está en inglés y que es mejor tener una aplicación que enseñe cómo crear hábitos porque de lo contrario uno puede empezar a crear un montón que luego no cumplirá y se terminará frustrando. author: Liam Dechery
developer_reply: Hello! So glad Habitica is working for you. For dailies, you have two options: 1, You can pause your dailies by checking into the inn, so you aren't penalized for any dailies you don't click. 2, You can edit the daily and change the start date -- that way it won't be due until that day. If you're still sick on that day, you can change it again. :)

text: ゲーム感覚のタスク管理アプリ。タスクをクリアするごとに、経験値やお金が手に入ります。ドット絵で描かれたキャラクターを着せ替えたり、ペットを育てて乗り物にしたり。ギルドやパーティで、同好の士とわいわい賑わったり、クエストを達成していくのもまた楽しい。ただスケジュール管理部分についてはやや弱いです。毎週や毎月の予定の繰り返し設定が弱く、また、タスクの色分けもできない(タスクの色は達成頻度や、タスク設定からの時間経過などで自動で決まってしまう)ため、あくまでもスケジュール管理アプリではなく、日々の目標を細かくこなしていくことへの達成感を得るためのアプリ、という感じ。ただ、ゲーム感覚で日課をこなしていく、という部分を、コツコツ積み上げていくのが合う人には、かなり楽しめるゲームだと思います。

text: ゲーム部分は遊んでおらず、「日課」を毎日自動でチェックオフしてくれるチェックリストとして使っています。 ★2の評価理由は、使用上かなり大きなストレスに感じる挙動があるためです。 このアプリを終了せずに別のアプリを使ったあとに再度このアプリを開くと、ときどき「日課が登録されていません」という表示になってしまうのです。上にスクロールしてリロードをしようとしてみても、リロードが完了せず、日課の一覧を確認できなくなってしまいます。 日課を再表示するためには一度アプリを終了してからもう一度アプリを起動する必要があります。時間にして5秒もかからない作業ではありますが、これが中々のストレスになっています。 日課が表示されなくなる現象の再現性はよく分かりません。別のアプリを開いていた時間なのか、別のアプリで負荷のかかる処理をした場合なのか、条件はよく分かりませんが、ちゃんと日課が表示されることもあります。体感的には40%程度日課が表示されなくなります。

text: App seems to be good at first. Beside obvious stuff, you have your character, you can equip new gear, gain new abilities etc., but after a while (~lvl 20) there is not much else to do. Of course, if you'll pay for diamonds with real money, that could change, but seriously, premium membership is ridiculously expensive

text: If you struggle with executive dysfunction and if you look for possibilities to change overwhelming tasks into play, that's right app for you! I use app for almost a week and I love it! It really helped me with long-waiting tasks and many of them are finally done! And it wasn't a pain. 😊 I also check my hydration level thanks to habit section. Dailies help to keep my routines in check and To-Do's are for spontaneous tasks appearing during the day. And pixel-art UI design is a cherry on the top!

Por si só, a funcionalidade de organizar hábitos, diárias e tarefas é simples e direta ao ponto, fácil o suficiente pra não ter muito trabalho para começar. A gamificação, com os itens e as missões em grupo, funciona maravilhosamente bem para gerar engajamento com as tarefas. Excelente comunidade! Parabéns 👏🏽👏🏽

text: Muito “brinquei” com os apps que gameficam a rotina e, com segurança de estar correto em meu veredito, decido e recomendo o Habitica como o melhor (com muita sobra).  Encontrei unicamente nele todos os clássicos recursos dos RPGs (sou da época de Chrono Trigger no SNES) sendo executados de maneira funcional; somente ele evolui o personagem (você) coerentemente e também o pune, tirando vida e até mesmo leveis; existe o uso de mana e classes; itens "dropam". Há um delicioso sistema de compra de equipamentos e armas, mascotes e montarias, há itens importantes e a sua organização das tarefas é de fato estimulante.  Como está escrito no próprio site: o que é um bom RPG sem chefões? Eles existem, são bem desenhados e você só os vence sendo rígido em sua rotina de tarefas, caso contrário seu personagem é ferido e mais quem do grupo o estiver enfrentando.  Não bastasse, encontrei no Habitica uma comunidade imensa de pessoas que contribuem uns com os outros para que você se torne melhor, gente que estimula; existe uma penca de desafios muito variados também.  Gostei tanto e estou-me beneficiando de tal maneira que assinei o serviço mesmo não sendo fundamental para o seu uso. O projeto e a comunidade são tão grandiosos que se você quiser, pode contribuir de muitas maneiras com os desenvolvimento e evolução do Habitica; pretendo no futuro ser um de seus colaboradores no desenvolvimento de suas graciosas pixels art. Habitica tornou-se minha ferramenta eleita para me ajudar a ser uma pessoa melhor, a correr atrás de meus sonhos.  5 estrela e nota 10, com louvor.

text: Este é o primeiro aplicativo do tipo que eu consigo usar consistentemente por meses, e no meu caso isso quer dizer muito. No começo, você pode se perguntar: “Qual a vantagem de adotar mais um item com o qual me preocupar, como cuidar de um bichinho virtual?”. Habitica é mais do que um Tamagoshi: esse aplicativo oferece uma motivação extra e divertida para fazer aquilo que você sabe que precisa fazer, e que vai ser bom para todo mundo. É claro que ele não pode se tornar a principal razão de cultivarmos bons hábitos, mas uma vez que tomemos esse cuidado, serve perfeitamente ao seu propósito. Habitica dá um panorama da sua agenda (e da sua vida) e o ajuda a enxergar o que é mais importante. Além disso, ele conta com uma comunidade muito simpática e em expansão, como numa rede social, onde você encontra pessoas exatamente como você, e desfruta um elemento indispensável no aperfeiçoamento pessoal: prestação de contas. Estou ansioso para ver todas a funções do aplicativo online disponíveis no app para smartphone. acontecer, vou dar um jeito de dar seis estrelas!

text: 這次更新寶石物品平白無故變貴 :( 用了將近一年說說優缺點。最大優點是跨平台支援，手機app網頁都可以用，支援網頁所以也可以用電腦開啟。電腦能下載外掛（插件）去擴充或修改一些設定。短期想訓練自己做到某件事很有用，長期的話遊戲內容不太足，大概練到100等就會發現機制單調化嚴重，遊戲沒有陪你繼續前進的感覺（或說不太夠）。伺服器有時很馬鈴薯，會勸退人的那種程度，建議不要讓玩家做什麼都要等伺服器回應，本來打開紀錄習慣只要10秒，馬鈴薯加成一開下去變成30秒還不斷回溯。訂閱方面算是佛心，一個寶石副本可以所有參與的人都能拿到獎勵。不過去年時曾寄給官方表示希望調整副本難度，單人太難、多人太不平衡，一兩位設立大量好習慣的法師可以輕易地秒殺所有副本，一兩位設立大量壞習慣的隊友可以輕易秒殺所有隊友（你沒聽錯就是這麼誇張），副本難度應該要根據人數與職業比例稍作調整，只要少數人勞動就可以的結果就是會發生社會怠惰的現象，對整個隊伍的運作來說很不好。打太多要爆字數ㄌ就這樣吧

text: 用這個app/網站七年了，已經成為自己生活習慣的一部分。中文翻譯有逐漸增多，但能看英文的話也能查到更多資源、可以和更多玩家互動。 因為自己本來就喜歡RPG遊戲，所以能一邊在現實中提升自己，一邊慢慢累積遊戲中的角色，應該是能讓我持續使用的關鍵點。最常用的是每日事項daily功能，很能幫助自己每天在特定目標上一點一點的累積。 從開始使用到現在，成就、功能等都有很多進步，整體的自由度也很高，可以用適合自己的方式來使用。有一段時間大多成就和寵物已蒐集完（沒課金的情況），就不太知道要做什麼，後來就創了自己的隊伍，以維持隊伍運作為目標繼續前進，也可以不時和夥伴們互相打氣；也用了重生球蒐集全職業裝備的成就、挑戰自己到達100等的速度；一邊用著google問卷獎勵來課金蒐集更多寵物。 驀然回首發現已經是這個軟體的老玩家(?)，現實中的自己也跟著它一點一點慢慢前進著，希望未來能開發更多玩法，繼續在這個世界冒險～ 也謝謝讓這個軟體運作的每個工作人員和志工。
